summary: An Indology and philosophy scholar, S. K. Ramanatha Sastri studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked as temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and as Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938.

An Indologist and historian, S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar earned his history degree and M.A. at the University of Madras. He lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History (~1921–1934).

An Indologist and philosopher, S. Kuppuswami Sastri studied at St. Peter's College, Tanjore, and the University of Madras, alongside traditional teachers Brahmendra Sarasvati and Nilakanta Sastri. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and later as Professor at Presidency College.

An Indologist, S. M. Natesa Sastri was educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Around 1884 to 1892, he worked as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.

Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, S. N. Balagangadhara studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch. He served as a director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
An Indologist, S. N. Krishna is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva.
An Indologist, S. N. Savadi held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, with affiliations attested in 1953 and 1969.
An Indologist, Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was affiliated with the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, where his positions are attested in 1939 and as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

An Indologist and archaeologist, S. Rajavelu served as Assistant Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and as Professor in the Department of Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).

An Indology and philosophy scholar, S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was affiliated with the University of Madras, where he served as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

An Indologist and historian, S. Sankaranarayanan was an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from around 1986 to 1999, and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

An Indologist, S. Sankararama Sastri served as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).

An Indologist and historian, S. Srikanta Sastri studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna from ~1923 to 1926. He subsequently held a post at the University of Mysore from ~1926 to 1960.
An Indologist and historian, S. Swaminathan studied under J. Sundaram. He served as Deputy Superintending Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India until retiring by 2013.

A scholar of religious studies and anthropology, Saba Mahmood studied at the University of Washington and completed her PhD at Stanford University (~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~1999–2004) and as Professor of sociocultural anthropology at UC Berkeley (2004–2018).
A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Sabine Klein-Schwind studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and is attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

An Indologist and philosopher, Sabine Löhr studied at the University of Freiburg and earned an M.A. at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen. She also worked as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.
Active in Tibetology, Sabriye Tenberken studied at the University of Bonn from ~1992 to 1997 and went on to found Braille Without Borders.

Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He later taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1957) and held a post at the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Working in computational linguistics and Indology, Sachin Kathale completed an M.Phil. at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and has worked as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.
